newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Cellnet to roam in China.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Cellnet to roam in China.

text.p: Cellnet, the mobile telephone company majority-owned by UK giant British Telecommunications Plc, said on Friday it was the first UK cellular operator to offer a roaming service to China.

The group said it hoped to offer the service within the next few weeks after signing an agreement with China Telecom, allowing around one million people on Cellnet's digital network to make and receive mobile telephone calls in most towns and cities in China.
Cellnet, 40-percent owned by Securicor Group Plc already offers a roaming service in 63 other countries spanning Europe, Scandinavia, the Middle East, parts of Asia and Hong Kong.
China has the third highest number of mobile telephone users in the world and is an increasingly popular destination for British business travellers and tourists, Cellnet said.
With one fifth of the world's population and one of the world's fastest rates of economic growth, China is a major target for UK business.

Cellnet has offered a service in Hong Kong since 1995. With the island due to revert back to Chinese control in three days, the new deal will allow Cellnet digital customers to use their mobile phones when travelling between the two territories.
